title: The Summons
text: “Oink.”
“Um, excuse me, Moto-san. Would you mind coming with us for a moment?”
Mole translated for me, I say.
“Yes? What is it?”
I feigned innocence and followed the pig that seemed to be their leader, I say. It led me down a deserted hallway. Suddenly, another pig doused me with a bucket of water.
“Hah! There we go,” it declared.
I elegantly dodged the water, and it splashed magnificently onto one of the summoner-pig’s companions standing behind me instead.
“Oi—?! Wha—?! OIIIIINK!”
The pig that got soaked by its own ambush shrieked in outrage at the unexpected dodge.
“Oink oink! Oink!”
“Why—why did it dodge?! Aim properly, you idiot! Is what it’s saying…”
“Kyaaaaa!”
Ho ho, time to raise a bigger fuss than that, I say.
“What’s going on? What happened?”
A crowd of male students came rushing over, startled by my scream.
“We were cleaning, and this poor thing got splashed with water—I was so surprised, I just screamed…”
“Ah, ah… I see, that explains it.”
“Oink… oink oink, oink!”
“Oink…”

After some pig made an excuse, they hauled the drenched pig away. Seems their little baptism attempt failed spectacularly. Honestly, did they really think something that pathetic could touch me? I say. When I returned to the classroom… well, the textbooks and bag I’d prepared as bait had bugs and small monster corpses stuffed inside, torn-up textbooks, and my school uniform in the locker shredded to ribbons. All exactly as planned, I say. I retrieved the recording crystals I’d set up beforehand—evidence secured, no doubt about it, I say. Still, just as expected, this academy—having once been attended by the Crimson Swine—has its rotten little corners well and truly rotten. Riska attended here too, so it’s not all bad, but the pigs’ turf wars make me want to vomit, I say. Itsuki had been lurking outside class hours and caught the perpetrators red-handed, footage from the recording crystal fully secured. And now, next up—a love letter waiting in the shoe locker, apparently. After school… someone’s waiting in front of the academy’s underground storeroom. Quite the classic confession spot, is it? Anyway, I headed to the scene, I say.
“…This is the place, I suppose.”
I waited there a while, and then…
“Oink oink oink.”
The same pigs who’d summoned me earlier gathered around, I say.
“Oh my, if it isn’t you lot from before. What business do you have with me?” I said, expecting some absurd accusation as usual.
“Heh heh heh… sorry, but we’re gonna have some fun at your expense.”
Oh? Seems some male students have joined the mix too, I say.
“Oink! Oiiink!”
Ah, spellcasting time.
“I, the wellspring of power, do command. Unravel the laws once more, and strike him numb, robbing him of freedom.”
That incantation… Zweite Paralyze, I say. But the weaving’s far too sloppy. Nothing more than what you’d expect from combat-inexperienced students, I say.
“Stay put, you—Zweite Paral—!”
“Anti-Zweite Paralyze!”
I nullified the spell those responding to the pig’s cue tried to cast, I say. Then, closing the distance with my spear collapsed into rod form, I stabbed them with Paralyze Lance.
“Ugh—!”
“No way—!”
Caught red-handed, I say. The thuggish-looking male student crumpled to the ground, paralyzed.
“Enough already, this is getting tiresome, pigs…”
Seems they wanted to bully the new transfer student, but they clearly don’t know their place, I say.
“Oink!?”
“OIIIINK!?”
“Time to ship these pigs off to slaughter, I saaaaay!”
No prying eyes here—perfect opportunity! I say, and skewered the pigs too with Paralyze Lance for good measure.
“O-oink?”
“Whoa! Wh-what on earth is going on here!”
Riska and Rafuemon showed up at this point. Were you two summoned here too, I wonder?
“Ah, pay it no mind. I’ll dispose of this lot posthaste, I say.”
“‘I say’? …No, wait, that doesn’t look remotely possible—”
I scooped up as many of the pig faction as my arms could carry, activated my Concealment Skill, and vanished from the scene, I say.
“Th-they disappeared! What in the world was that just now…”
“Ah, Rafuemon-san. Please don’t worry about that person.”

Itsuki answered, though only his voice came through—seems he’d been operating alongside Riska. And thus, one particularly excessive strain of pus was dealt with, I say. Predictably, the pig in question turned out to be from a noble family and tried to play victim, leaning on its household’s influence, but the moment its parent showed up, I performed a costume change and revealed myself as Spear Hero. The once-haughty parent instantly turned to groveling, even begging for its life. Expulsion proceedings followed at record speed, I hear.
Now, this is footage recorded by Itsuki’s crystal.
“Bwehhh…”
“Oink-oink oink oink!”
“Oink!”
“That’s completely unreasonable! Why should Rishia-chan have to go along with that!”
Rafuemon protested, but the pigs, utterly indifferent, shoved him aside.
“Violence is bad! Trying to solve everything with violence isn’t okay! Itsuki-kun doesn’t belong to any of you!”
Seems Rafuemon had been trying to shield Riska from something.
“You’d be better off not making me or Rishia-chan angry, y’know!”
“Bwehhh! Bwe-bwe! Bwe!”
The cornered Riska apparently fired back quite the retort.
“Oink!”
A pig lunged to strike, but Riska smoothly dodged and countered, sending it tumbling to the ground.
“OIIIIIIIINK!”
Taking that as a cue to “get her,” the surrounding pigs began chanting spells at Riska—but she wasn’t about to let that opening slip by, I say.
“Bwehhhh.”
Riska swiftly loosed Wing Blow at all their bellies to keep them in check. She’s grown stronger, sure, but still holding back an awful lot, I say.
“Bwiiiiiiii!”
Taking that as resistance, the pigs apparently escalated into Drifa-class incantations. Well, still well within what Riska and Rafuemon could handle, I say.
“That’s quite enough, everyone.”
Itsuki dropped his concealment and revealed himself here, I say. The pigs’ faces reportedly bloomed with the very color of shock.
“I did warn you that violence and bullying wouldn’t be tolerated, yet it seems the message didn’t sink in at all. The lot of you—rest assured, this incident will be thoroughly reported.”
Itsuki gently guided Riska away, hand placed protectively at her side.
“Oink! Oink! Oink-oink!”

“No matter how many words you pile up, I’ve been watching your actions from the very start. Remember this well: heroes can also serve justice by watching quietly, unseen. I heard your true feelings loud and clear.”
“OIIIIIIIIIIIIINK!”
A tremendous pig-scream reportedly echoed through the air. Apparently, it was claiming this was all a misunderstanding.
“Rishia-san, Rafuemon-san. Sorry about this. Now then, please head to your next summons.”
“Bwehhhh…”
“I’d heard you were draining the pus, but wow, that’s something else. Itsuki-kun, are you doing okay?”

“Yes, I suppose first impressions matter most. Motoyasu-san says there are far craftier ones out there, but if there are this many summons on the very first day, exactly how many factions does this academy have…? Those vying for the position of hero’s girlfriend truly are terrifying.”

Naofumi-sama is amazing, Itsuki muttered for some reason at this point. From there, Riska and Rafuemon were summoned yet again, this time in front of the academy’s clock tower. And of course, pigs and men had set another trap there too.
“Oink!”
“Heh heh heh… Rishia Ivyred. Nothing personal, but we’re gonna have ourselves some fun.”
Plenty of lowlife male students here too, it seems. Quite the fitting academy for Itsuki, I say.
“Bwehhh.”
“Rishia-chan, I think I’m starting to get used to this.”
Rafuemon wore an exasperated look, the kind reserved for something pitiable. Compared to the warmth in his eyes when looking at Itsuki, this was positively subzero.
“Hold it right theeere!”
Th-that voice! It’s Fleon-chan, I say!
“Ahh… you already caught wind of this? Or rather, the culprit is clearly Motoyasu-san. No doubt about it. Rafuemon-san!”
Even while hidden, Itsuki muttered under his breath, I say. Concealment skills sorely lacking!
“Yep!”
Rafuemon began patting his belly, pom pom.
